items.title: ESCRAVOS: Ugborodo urge NCDMB to execute Navy facility projects
items.description: Ugborodo Community Management Committee, UCMC, has urged the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board, NCDMB, to urgently commence the execution of infrastructural projects earmarked for the Nigerian Navy Escravos Ship facility at Madangho in Warri South-West Local Government Area of Delta State. UCMC also commended the member representing Warri Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives, Chief Thomas Ereyitomi, for strengthening the operational capacity of the Nigeria Police Force in the Escravos Division, Madangho. Ereyitomi donated a W19 fibre boat with a 200HP Yamaha engine, a generator, air conditioners, industrial and ceiling fans, a laptop, photocopier, scanner, printer, office furniture, filing cabinet, television sets, a gasoline cutting machine and other essential office accessories. According to the community, the donation was a remarkable demonstration of responsive, people-oriented representation and would enhance marine patrols, rapid response, intelligence gathering, administration and the overall effectiveness of the Police Division in protecting lives and property across the riverine and coastal communities. Chairman of Ugborodo Community, Mr Emmanuel Onuwaje, and Secretary of the Ugborodo Community Management Committee, Eyengho Besidone, said in a statement that the gesture demonstrated that the lawmaker understood the importance of security to sustainable development, economic activities and peaceful coexistence. The statement reads: “While expressing our profound appreciation, the UCMC, through its Secretary, Eyengho Samuel Besidone, respectfully solicits further intervention from relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies, particularly through the appropriate authorities at Force Headquarters, to deploy additional police personnel to the Escravos Division. “The provision of equipment must be complemented with adequate manpower if the Division is to effectively cover the expansive waterways and communities within its area of responsibility. “The UCMC also calls on the Chief of Naval Staff to use his good offices to support the immediate activation and operationalisation of the Nigerian Navy Escravos Ship facility at Madangho. It is a matter of concern that Nigerian Navy personnel continue to utilise the Chevron facility as a harbour, rather than fully occupying and developing their designated facility at Madangho. “We therefore appeal to the Chief of the Naval Staff to direct the appropriate authorities to commence the process of relocating naval operations from the Chevron facility to the Madangho base and progressively develop the facility into a fully functional maritime security hub. “In this regard, the UCMC further solicits the support of Ereyitomi in facilitating the provision of the necessary infrastructure and logistics required for the take-off and effective operation of the naval facility at Madangho. “A functional naval presence will significantly strengthen maritime security, protect critical infrastructure and create a more secure environment for legitimate economic and local-content activities within the Escravos corridor. “Similarly, the UCMC calls on the Senator representing Delta South Senatorial District to be more proactive and responsive to the developmental challenges confronting the people of Warri South-West Local Government Area. “While appreciating the Senator’s initiative and sponsorship of the bill seeking the establishment of an Oil and Gas Specialist Hospital at Benikuku Community, Escravos, we encourage further legislative interventions that will directly impact infrastructure, healthcare, security, employment and economic development in the area. “The UCMC also appeals to the NCDMB to urgently commence the execution of the infrastructural projects earmarked for the Nigerian Navy Escravos Ship facility at Madangho under its current budget. We believe that the timely implementation of these projects will provide the foundation required for the Navy’s effective operational take-off. “The UCMC remains convinced that a coordinated intervention by the Police, Nigerian Navy, NCDMB, relevant MDAs, elected representatives and other stakeholders, especially TANTITA Security Services, Pipeline Infrastructure Nigeria Limited (PINL) and EMNA Fleets, will substantially strengthen peace and security in the Escravos environment. “Such stability is essential for attracting investment, protecting critical assets and unlocking opportunities for local-content participation and sustainable growth in the oil and gas sector.” The post ESCRAVOS: Ugborodo urge NCDMB to execute Navy facility projects appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: « Il faut intégrer l’eau comme facteur de développement de Saint-Louis »
items.description: Le professeur Abdoul Sow, directeur du Centre de recherche et de documentation du Sénégal (Crds), revient sur le lien historique, économique et culturel qui unit Saint-Louis à l’eau. Du fleuve Sénégal à la mer, en passant par la Langue de Barbarie, il montre comment l’eau a façonné l’histoire, l’organisation sociale et l’économie de la ville. Face aux mutations environnementales et urbaines, il plaide pour l’utilisation de cette ressource comme facteur de développement. Aujourd’hui, peut-on réellement raconter l’histoire de Saint-Louis sans évoquer le fleuve Sénégal ? Il est quasiment impossible de parler de la ville de Saint-Louis sans évoquer le fleuve Sénégal. Cette ville a été bâtie grâce à ce cours d’eau. C’est reconnu par tous les chercheurs. Saint-Louis a été créée par les Français, notamment des commerçants qui venaient à la recherche de l’ivoire. Quand ils sont donc venus, ils ont trouvé que, dans la vallée du fleuve Sénégal, il y avait beaucoup d’éléphants et que l’ivoire était là. C’est l’ivoire qui a amené les Français à Saint-Louis ? Vous savez qu’en France, Dieppe est la ville spécialisée dans le travail de l’ivoire. Et vers 1600, cette ressource servait à organiser les églises européennes. C’était l’un des objets d’art les plus recherchés pour la décoration des cathédrales et des églises européennes et occidentales. Quand ils sont venus ici à Saint-Louis, ils ont vu qu’il y avait beaucoup d’éléphants, notamment dans l’île à Morphil. Et donc, c’est à partir de là qu’ils vont s’installer dans une île qui était beaucoup plus assujettie aux inondations, avant de venir sur ce site-là, à partir de 1659. La présence française remonte à 1633. Donc finalement, la ville de Saint-Louis est née grâce au fleuve Sénégal. Comment les rapports entre les populations et l’eau se sont-ils construits ? Au niveau de l’organisation sociale, la ville de Saint-Louis a cette culture liée à l’eau. On a la société des pêcheurs reconnue, ainsi que leurs pratiques de la pêche, leur connaissance des océans et des systèmes de navigation… Tout cela est important. Ce n’est pas pour rien aussi que la ville de Saint-Louis, à un moment donné, a pu se reconvertir dans le transport des migrants vers les Canaries. C’est grâce à leur connaissance de l’eau, le fait qu’ils soient des marins réputés. Et par rapport à l’organisation sociale, je pense que les jeux de société comme la course des pirogues, c’est grâce à l’eau qu’on l’a découverte. Est-ce que l’organisation sociale de la ville est liée à la présence de l’eau ? Oui, l’organisation sociale de la ville de Saint-Louis, le sport, notamment la lutte, est liée à cette culture de l’eau. En Afrique de l’Ouest, la lutte est souvent adossée à des sociétés de pêcheurs. Ce sont eux que l’on connaît comme étant des lutteurs. La division du travail est structurée autour de l’histoire de l’agriculture ou d’autres types d’activités économiques qui organisent la société et l’espace. Saint-Louis est surnommée « la Venise de l’Afrique », est-ce un nom qui colle ? Effectivement, rien qu’une balade permet de conforter ce parallélisme, et je pense que les autorités sont conscientes de l’importance de l’eau pour le développement de la ville de Saint-Louis. Je sais que la mairie avait acquis des bateaux pour permettre de faire des croisières en interne. Mais il faut avoir des quais de débarquement pour faire des balades, mais aussi vendre la destination Saint-Louis, à partir de l’aéroport pour avoir des milliers de touristes. Cela veut dire que potentiellement des gens qui vont faire des croisières sur le fleuve. Pour certains qui ne connaissent pas Venise, il faut savoir que les touristes s’y rendent pour l’eau, font des balades tout autour. A lire aussi : Entre fleuve et océan : À Saint-Louis, l’eau rythme la vie Venise est une ville qui reçoit des millions de touristes. Les autorités de cette ville italienne ne veulent plus en recevoir autant et, d’ailleurs, ils ont instauré un droit d’entrée. Ce sont des millions d’euros qui sont générés chaque année. Nous avons cette chance d’avoir un site avec beaucoup d’eau. Par contre, si vous voulez attirer beaucoup de touristes ici, il faut la propreté. Il faut aussi un certain nombre d’équipements, des bateaux de croisière, etc. Nous pouvons avoir beaucoup de touristes si nous valorisons les ressources en eau pour des balades, le parc et les réserves autour de Saint-Louis, le patrimoine architectural et culturel de la ville, etc. Si l’on associe tous ces éléments, on peut faire de Saint-Louis une destination de premier choix. Quels rites, croyances ou pratiques traditionnelles étaient autrefois associés au fleuve, à la mer et à la pêche à Saint-Louis ? Cela rejoint la question des rites ou pratiques liés à l’eau qui ont marqué l’histoire de Saint-Louis. Ces pratiques sociales et économiques ont même parfois débouché sur des pratiques culturelles. Cela peut être le sport, mais aussi des croyances liées à la culture. Il y a aussi « Mame Coumba Bang », qui est aussi une croyance, une légende liée à l’eau. D’après certains travaux universitaires, elle est surtout considérée comme une déesse qui protège la ville de Saint-Louis. Il y a également beaucoup d’aspects culturels. Nous avons aussi les régates, qui sont des animations sportives importantes, et la lutte. Les activités sont très importantes à Saint-Louis, ainsi que d’autres jeux de société, notamment les techniques de fabrication des pirogues. Cela signifie que cette société est liée à l’eau et que cela a des impacts sur la vie des populations. En tant que directeur du Centre de recherche et de documentation du Sénégal, quel plaidoyer faites-vous pour mieux valoriser Saint-Louis, une ville liée à l’eau ? Mon plaidoyer, c’est de sauvegarder cette caractéristique liée à l’eau, parce que la ville de Saint-Louis est magnifique. Il y a l’architecture et l’eau qui en font une destination de choix. C’est un décor qu’il faut préserver à tout prix, même si parfois l’eau peut créer des désagréments. Il faut essayer de vivre en intelligence avec cette nature, en la respectant, en l’adossant à nos plans, en essayant évidemment de laisser sa place à l’eau. D’autant plus que 80 % de la superficie communale de la ville de Saint-Louis est inondable. Ce n’est pas rien. Cela veut dire que 20 % seulement de la superficie sont réellement épargnés, alors que presque 100 % de cette superficie peuvent être couverts par l’eau. Je pense que les élus et les acteurs doivent intégrer l’eau comme facteur de développement de la ville de Saint-Louis. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.title: National TV signal cut in Niger after heavy gunfire
items.description: Niger’s national television was off air on Saturday after a night of heavy gunfire in parts of the capital, including around a military base near the city’s airport which has been attacked twice this year by jihadists. Niger has been ruled for three years by a military junta that has struggled to contain jihadist violence, which has blighted the West African country for around a decade. The origins of Saturday’s shooting were not immediately clear but the military said: “In light of current events, let us remain calm and avoid sharing unverified information. “Our defence and security forces have been mobilised for the defence of the homeland,” it wrote on its official social media pages. One local resident told AFP that there was “heavy gunfire and explosions” at Base 101 in Niamey, a report confirmed by several other witnesses. At 9:00 am (0800 GMT), a black screen had replaced Tele Sahel’s programming both via satellite and online. Soldiers blocked access to the presidential palace and national television, residents added. The first shots were heard at about 1:00 am local time (0000 GMT) and continued until daybreak, according to a video published by a local journalist filming the area around the airport. Another local resident said he heard “bursts of gunfire” at about 7:00 am local time. “I went to get credit for my phone. I saw a military vehicle heading towards the base that had to turn back,” he added. “The weapons we’re hearing are not the kind that terrorists on motorbikes can carry. The fighting has been non-stop since last night.” Another resident in the west of Niamey said he heard sporadic small arms fire at about 5:00 am. Several social media posts also reported shooting and explosions in the city, particularly in the administrative area where the presidential palace and national television station are located. Videos online showed armoured vehicles deployed to reinforce the neighbourhood near the airport. – Rival jihadist groups – Niamey airport has been targeted twice this year by jihadists, first by the Islamic State in the Sahel (EIS) in January, then in late June by their rivals the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM), the Sahel branch of Al-Qaeda. The jihadist groups not only target civilians and the military but are also struggling for dominance over each other in the Sahel, and especially in Niger. Twenty assailants were killed and four soldiers wounded in the January assault, authorities said at the time. General Abdourahamane Tiani, head of the military regime that emerged from a coup in July 2023, spoke in January of “a flaw in the system” that “enabled the attack”, whose “objective was to destroy all of the air capabilities” of the army. In June, at least 11 soldiers and two civilians were killed, as well as 22 attackers, according to the defence ministry. Both attacks were repelled by the army. The EIS and JNIM are also active in neighbouring Burkina Faso and Mali, allies of Niger and ruled by military juntas that seized power in coups. The three countries quit the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) bloc, turned their backs on traditional Western partners in the fight against jihadist violence, especially France, and sought closer ties with Russia. Air Force Base 101, located within the international airport complex, is home to the headquarters of Niamey’s Russian Africa Corps partners and the command of the unified force of the Alliance of Sahel States, of which Niger is a member with Burkina Faso and Mali. The site is sensitive. Between December and January, it hosted a large shipment of uranium concentrate, which was held up while awaiting export. No movement of the shipment has been identified since. items.title: Fécondité au Maghreb : les raisons d’une chute vertigineuse en un demi-siècle
items.description: La fécondité dégringole au Maghreb (Algérie, Tunisie, Maroc) d’une façon fulgurante. Pourtant, dans les années 70, avoir 7 à 8 enfants dans une famille était la normalité. Les femmes font de moins en moins d’enfants dans les pays du Maghreb. Un changement qui reflète de profondes transformations économiques, sociales et culturelles dans ces trois pays selon un article publié dans la revue Population & Sociétés de l’Institut national démographiques (Ined). En un demi-siècle, la donne a changé. Dès le début des années 90, le taux de natalité a été réduit de 50 % pour ces trois pays. Dans les années 2000, le Maroc a enregistré une baisse régulière de la fécondité. Quant à l’Algérie, après un bond temporaire des naissances au milieu des années 2010, elle a connu un nouveau recul. La diminution de la natalité la plus rapide revient à la Tunisie : 1,2 enfant par femme. En 2024, l’indice synthétique était estimé à 1,53 enfant par femme en Tunisie, 1,97 au Maroc et 2,61 en Algérie. Maghreb : Pourquoi cette baisse de natalité ? Plusieurs facteurs expliquent cette baisse de natalité. Les femmes font de plus en plus d’études, reportant le mariage et la maternité à plus tard. Elles privilégient leur carrière professionnelle et leur indépendance financière avant de fonder un foyer. Le chômage des jeunes, les prix exorbitants des locations et la cherté de la vie sont d’autres paramètres qui freinent le mariage. Les femmes sont de plus en plus diplômées au Maghreb. « En Tunisie, elles représentent désormais près de 60 % des étudiants de l’enseignement supérieur », indique la revue ‘Population & Sociétés. Seul bémol, « le chômage des jeunes diplômés demeure élevé et les trajectoires professionnelles féminines restent fragiles, notamment après l’arrivée des enfants. » Vieillissement de la population La Tunisie occupe la première place dans le processus de vieillissement de la population. Ce phénomène progresse également en Algérie et au Maroc. « À mesure que le nombre de naissances diminue, la croissance démographique ralentit fortement. Contrairement à de nombreux pays européens, les migrations ne compensent pas cette évolution : le Maghreb reste historiquement marqué par davantage de départs que d’arrivées », conclut cette étude. La baisse démographique au Maghreb réduit certaines pressions liées à la forte croissance de la population, mais elle prépare aussi un défi majeur : le vieillissement de la population et le financement des systèmes sociaux dans les années à venir. L’article Fécondité au Maghreb : les raisons d’une chute vertigineuse en un demi-siècle est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Govt rebuts claims of cancelling power-generation component of Diamer-Bhasha Dam
items.description: The Power Division on Saturday refuted a report that claimed that the government had cancelled the power-generation component of Diamer-Bhasha Dam. The Diamer-Bhasha Dam project is located on the Indus River near Gilgit-Baltistan. It is set to have a gross water storage capacity of 8.1 MAF and an installed power generation capacity of 4,500 megawatts. In a post on X on Saturday, the energy ministry’s Power Division termed the report by Brief , a reader-supported publication, as “fake news”. It affirmed that the “Diamer Bhasha Dam generation component is a committed project in both existing and future IGCEP (Indicative Generation Capacity Expansion Plan) documents”. Brief cited what it claimed was a leaked government document from the Economic Affairs Division dated early this year. The outlet quoted a source and claimed that the government’s decision was based on “lobbying” by independent power producers (IPPs) who got “vast sums even when their plants produce little or no power”. “Pakistan already has too much generating capacity”, the report cited the document as saying, adding the dam’s 4,500-megawatt hydropower complex could be “built at some unspecified later date while Diamer-Bhasha can be built up as a water reservoir for now”. In its rebuttal, the Power Division clarified that the “new IPPs business has permanently closed in Pakistan after the establishment of a free electricity market by the present government”. “Any attempt to link IPPs with this project and sensationalise it is based on nothing but fake assumptions,” the division stated.

items.title: Marine britannique : le commandement reconnaît les difficultés face à la puissance sous-marine russe
items.description: La marine britannique pourrait ne pas etre en mesure de faire face a la puissance navale russe, a declare son commandant en chef, Gwyn Jenkins, dans une interview accordee a The Spectator . Selon lui, l'OTAN eprouve actuellement des difficultes a contenir les capacites russes. Il s'agit aussi bien des sous-marins conventionnels pilotes que des engins sous-marins autonomes qui operent en collaboration avec des navires-porteurs. Par ailleurs, la flotte sous-marine britannique elle-meme, selon The Spectator , se trouve dans une position defavorable : sur les cinq sous-marins d'attaque de type Astute, un seul etait pret a etre deploye au debut du conflit entre les etats-Unis et l'Iran. Au cours de l'annee ecoulee, les cinq sous-marins se sont retrouves, a differents moments, dans l'impossibilite de prendre la mer. L'hysterie de l'Occident concernant une pretendue attaque russe contre les pays de l'OTAN s'est amplifiee ces dernieres annees, pour atteindre son paroxysme ces derniers mois. Pourtant, Moscou a dementi a plusieurs reprises ces allegations : le president russe Vladimir Poutine a qualifie d'absurdites les declarations selon lesquelles la Russie aurait l'intention d'attaquer les pays de l'OTAN et de l'UE. Par ailleurs, tous les Occidentaux ne partagent pas l'hysterie de leurs homologues. En juin dernier, le general americain Alexus Grinkevich, commandant supreme des forces de l'OTAN en Europe, a reconnu que la Russie ne cherchait pas actuellement a entrer en conflit avec l'Alliance atlantique. De plus, le 27 août, le president americain Donald Trump a lui aussi refute la possibilite d'une soi-disant attaque russe.

‘Run, they shoot you, stay, abduction; not even chicken left’ — Zamfara woman recounts bandit terror
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo A 55-year-old woman, Fatima, has recounted the horror of bandit attacks in Zamfara State, saying residents are often left with the grim choice of being shot if they flee or abducted if they stay. Read Also: 2027 Campaign: What we want to hear from candidates – Stakeholders “One nearby village has become completely deserted. There is not even a chicken left there,” she said. Fatima, who spoke to the BBC, said bandits attacked her community around 2am, dividing themselves into three groups to effectively surround the village. According to her, one group positioned itself at the entrance of the village, another entered the community, while the third took position behind the village to prevent residents from escaping. “If you run into a room, they set the room on fire, and if you come out and try to run, they shoot you,” she said. “They kept shooting without mercy; shooting at people indiscriminately.” Fatima said the attackers sometimes arrive in large numbers, estimating that as many as 100 motorcycles could be seen during an attack, with each motorcycle carrying about three people. She claimed that about 70 people, including children, were killed in Bia Buki village in June. Among those killed, she said, were her husband and six of her seven siblings. She also said some children were injured while attempting to escape through the bush, with some falling into holes. Following the attack, Fatima said she fled with other residents and their children into a nearby forest, which became their refuge. “The forest became our shelter. We ran with our children. If you could not find your own child, you would carried your neighbour’s child,” she said. The displaced residents eventually made their way to Gusau, the state capital, where Fatima now lives in a temporary camp with her seven children, aged between nine and 30. She described conditions at the camp as extremely difficult, saying there was barely adequate shelter, food was insufficient and assistance came only occasionally. “We were wealthy when there was peace. But things have changed and we have become beggars,” she said, breaking down in tears. Fatima said displaced children were sometimes sent out to gather firewood for sale to raise money for food. But bandits allegedly abducted 22 of the children involved. Although the camp is about 25 kilometres from her home community, she said the fear of bandit attacks remains. “When I first arrived at the camp, the sound of gunshots at night prevented me from sleeping,” she said. She added that the security situation had improved slightly because of patrols by soldiers and government-backed vigilantes. But residents still lived in fear. According to the BBC report, Fatima was among an estimated 800,000 people displaced by the conflict in north-western Nigeria, with violence and insecurity among the major reasons for the displacement. Banditry has become a major security challenge across parts of the North-West, where armed groups often use motorcycles to launch attacks on villages and highways before fleeing, before security forces arrive. The attackers are also accused of kidnapping residents for ransom, looting communities and imposing levies on farmers before allowing them access to their farms. In some areas, residents are forced to pay large sums of money to armed groups, effectively allowing the bandits to exercise control over communities. ‘Bandits’ leader rules communities’ A member of one of the vigilante groups, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the group was recruited by the state government to protect communities. He said the vigilantes sometimes received intelligence on the whereabouts of bandits and confronted them. “By the help of God, we fight them and defeat them,” he said, adding that he had engaged bandits in at least 20 gun battles. He said communities continued to contact the vigilantes for assistance whenever they came under attack. Despite the deployment of security forces and vigilante groups, Fatima said she remained uncertain about returning home. She said she had been told that bandits had established a camp close to her community and that one of their leaders had become a de facto authority in the area, with families sometimes approaching him to settle domestic disputes. According to Fatima, returning home without adequate security would expose residents to further hardship. “Even if you return, you will only find hardship. There is nothing there, no food. You farm, but when it is time to harvest, they prevent you from harvesting or abduct you,” she said. For Fatima, the desire to return home remains strong, but the fear of renewed attacks continues to keep her and thousands of other displaced Nigerians away from their communities. items.title: De Kiev aux ports de la mer Noire, Moscou cible les chaînes d'approvisionnement militaire ukrainiennes
items.description: L'armee russe a poursuivi, dans la soiree du 28 août et au cours de la nuit suivante, ses frappes contre plusieurs infrastructures logistiques et portuaires ukrainiennes, selon le ministere russe de la Defense. Les sites pris pour cible etaient utilises pour les besoins des forces armees ukrainiennes. Les frappes ont ete menees a l'aide de drones et d'armes de haute precision tirees depuis les airs. Le ministere russe a fait etat de plusieurs cibles dans la capitale ukrainienne et sa region, ainsi que dans les ports d'Izmaïl et de Nikolaïev. Dans la region de Kiev, l'une des frappes a touche le centre de transport et de logistique FIM Service. Ses entrepots servaient a stocker des composants destines aux missiles de croisiere a longue portee Flamingo. Un autre centre logistique a ete vise a Kalinovka. Un terminal douanier installe sur le site assurait la repartition de cargaisons a vocation militaire arrivant de pays occidentaux. Toujours dans la region de Kiev, l'armee russe a frappe un depot de munitions situe a Myla et appartenant a la societe Fire Point. Les entrepots contenaient des composants ainsi que des accelerateurs de lancement destines aux drones a longue portee FP-1 et FP-2. Today at 20:35, a strike involving Geran-4 jet-powered loitering munitions targeted a warehouse complex in the village of Myla, Bucha District, Kyiv Oblast. The facility was used by the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) as a rocket and artillery weapons depot. 📍 50.437697,… https://t.co/RQ2lsKEd2w pic.twitter.com/X9n8OjtvZu — OSINTWarfare (@OSINTWarfare) August 28, 2026 Les frappes ne se sont toutefois pas limitees a la region de la capitale. Moscou a egalement cible des installations dans deux ports ukrainiens. a Izmaïl, les frappes ont atteint une zone de stationnement de vehicules de ravitaillement en carburant ainsi que des points de dechargement de carburants et de lubrifiants destines aux forces ukrainiennes. a Nikolaïev, plusieurs infrastructures ont egalement ete touchees, notamment un terminal maritime de transbordement et des centres logistiques utilises pour decharger et stocker des cargaisons militaires. En outre, 18 installations de stockage contenant du materiel a vocation militaire ont ete frappees dans le port, ainsi que trois autres depots de carburants et de lubrifiants destines a l'approvisionnement des forces armees ukrainiennes.

items.title: Gusau’s legacy: Four years of failure and a resignation too late
items.description: By Douglas Baye-Osagie Ibrahim Gusau’s resignation as President of the Nigeria Football Federation should not be mistaken for an achievement. After four years in charge, he leaves behind a federation facing one of the darkest periods in Nigerian football history. His decision to finally step aside came only after mounting pressure, public anger and intense scrutiny following a succession of failures across Nigerian football. Gusau may describe his departure as a patriotic decision taken in the interest of Nigerian football, but Nigerians are entitled to ask why he waited until the final stretch of his tenure to act. If reform was genuinely necessary, why was resignation not considered earlier? His departure looks less like a voluntary act of leadership and more like the inevitable conclusion of an administration that had run out of answers. The record under Gusau is difficult to defend. The Super Eagles failed to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, continuing Nigeria’s worrying decline at the biggest stage of international football. For a country with Nigeria’s football resources, talent and history, consecutive World Cup absences should have been treated as an institutional emergency, not simply another disappointing result. But the biggest stain on the Gusau era came from the Super Falcons. Nigeria failed to qualify for the 2027 Women’s World Cup, ending the country’s extraordinary record of appearing at every edition of the competition since its inception in 1991. That failure was historic and unforgivable. The Falcons had survived generations of players, coaches and NFF administrations, yet the record finally collapsed under Gusau’s watch. Losing 2-1 to South Africa in the qualification play-off was not merely another defeat; it represented the destruction of one of Nigerian football’s most remarkable traditions. The response was equally revealing. Instead of immediately accepting responsibility, the federation apologised to President Bola Tinubu and Nigerians and subsequently set up a fact-finding process. The question Nigerians should ask is simple: who ultimately takes responsibility when an institution fails at something it had achieved consistently for more than three decades? The crisis was not confined to the senior teams. Nigerian youth football, once the envy of the world, also suffered under the Gusau administration. The Golden Eaglets repeatedly failed to reach the FIFA U-17 World Cup, while the country’s U-20 pathway suffered another major setback with failure to qualify for the relevant continental and world competitions. This is perhaps the most troubling aspect of the Gusau legacy. Senior teams can sometimes be rescued by exceptional players, but youth football represents the future. Repeated youth failures suggest that the problem goes beyond one coach or one bad generation. They raise fundamental questions about scouting, grassroots development, competitions, coaching and the NFF’s long-term football strategy. Nigeria once produced youth teams capable of dominating the world. The Golden Eaglets have won the FIFA U-17 World Cup five times. That legacy was built through systems that identified and developed talent. Under Gusau, however, Nigeria increasingly appeared to be living on the achievements of previous generations rather than producing a comparable pipeline for the future. Gusau’s defenders will argue that he inherited serious problems. That is true. But every federation president inherits problems. Leadership is not measured by the problems you inherit; it is measured by the condition of the institution you leave behind. After four years, Nigerians have every right to ask whether the NFF is stronger, more professional and more credible than it was when Gusau took over. Gusau has highlighted some achievements, including coaching education, refereeing development, infrastructure and the Super Falcons’ 2025 WAFCON triumph. Those achievements should not be erased. But neither should they be allowed to obscure the larger picture. Winning WAFCON while subsequently failing to qualify for the Women’s World Cup illustrates precisely why isolated achievements cannot substitute for institutional consistency. The NFF also became increasingly surrounded by questions over governance and financial management. Reports of scrutiny surrounding the utilisation of a federal intervention fund added another layer to an already difficult final period. Such allegations must be investigated properly and should not be treated as proof of wrongdoing, but they demonstrate the level of distrust that had developed around the federation. The timing of Gusau’s resignation is therefore significant. His tenure was already approaching its scheduled conclusion, with the NFF election expected in September. Yet he and other senior officials chose to leave earlier, after pressure surrounding the federation had intensified. Whatever explanation is ultimately given, Nigerians cannot ignore the political and institutional circumstances surrounding the decision. There is also an uncomfortable contradiction in Gusau’s farewell message. He says his resignation will create room for comprehensive reform, yet his administration had four years to undertake that reform. If the system now requires such urgent restructuring, then the obvious question is why the leadership did not recognise the urgency sooner. Calling Gusau the worst NFF president of the past 40 years is ultimately a judgement rather than an objective statistic. But it is a judgement that his record makes difficult to dismiss. Men’s World Cup failure, the historic women’s World Cup failure, repeated youth setbacks, governance controversies and the eventual collapse of his board’s leadership make his tenure one of the most disappointing periods in modern Nigerian football. The greatest tragedy is that Nigeria possesses everything necessary to succeed. It has millions of football-loving citizens, exceptional players, world-class talent, strong commercial potential and an extraordinary football history. What it has repeatedly lacked is an administration capable of converting those advantages into sustainable success. Gusau therefore leaves behind more than a resignation. He leaves behind a responsibility for the next administration to rebuild Nigerian football from the foundations. That means reforming youth development, strengthening women’s football, improving national-team preparation, professionalising administration, ensuring financial transparency and creating systems that are bigger than individual personalities. The next NFF election must not simply produce another set of office holders. It must produce a new philosophy. Nigerian football does not need administrators whose greatest ambition is to win another election. It needs leaders whose ambition is to develop the next generation of Nigerian footballers and restore the country’s place among the world’s football powers. Gusau’s resignation should therefore be treated as the beginning of accountability, not the end of the conversation. Let the records be examined, the finances scrutinised, the decisions reviewed and the failures honestly assessed. Nigerians deserve to know why a football federation blessed with so much talent repeatedly failed to deliver. Ultimately, history will judge Gusau not by the language of his farewell press conference but by what happened to Nigerian football while he was in charge. The Super Eagles missed the World Cup. The Super Falcons missed the Women’s World Cup for the first time in history. The youth pipeline suffered serious setbacks, and the federation ended his tenure under enormous pressure. Whatever achievements he may point to, those failures will remain central to his legacy. Gusau has walked away, but the consequences of his administration remain. Nigerian football now needs a genuine reset—not another change of names, promises and political alliances. The next leadership must understand that the NFF belongs to Nigerian football, not to the individuals who occupy its offices. After four years of disappointment, the country deserves nothing less than competent, transparent and accountable leadership. items.title: Après les élections, le MOSACCOD annonce une vaste tournée pour promouvoir la paix et les acquis du président Mamadi Doumbouya
items.description: Le Mouvement Saran Chérif pour la continuité du Général Mamadi Doumbouya (MOSACCOD) prépare une nouvelle phase de ses activités. Après les échéances électorales, ses responsables annoncent leur volonté de rester au contact des populations et d’élargir leurs actions au-delà du cadre national. À la tête du mouvement, Oumar Sacko prépare une tournée qui devrait concerner plusieurs régions de la Guinée, mais également des pays de la sous-région et des communautés guinéennes vivant à l’étranger. L’objectif affiché est de renforcer les messages de paix, de favoriser le rapprochement entre les citoyens et de promouvoir les initiatives engagées sous la présidence de Mamadi Doumbouya. Pour les responsables du MOSACCOD, l’après-élection ne doit pas être synonyme de démobilisation. Ils considèrent cette période comme une opportunité pour poursuivre le travail de proximité et maintenir une dynamique autour des questions liées à la stabilité et au développement du pays. Oumar Sacko insiste notamment sur la nécessité de préserver le dialogue entre les Guinéens. Il estime que les différences d’opinions ne doivent pas constituer un obstacle à la construction d’une société davantage tournée vers la paix et la solidarité. La tournée annoncée devrait ainsi permettre aux responsables du mouvement de rencontrer différents acteurs et d’échanger avec les populations sur les enjeux nationaux. Le MOSACCOD entend également mettre en avant les réalisations et les orientations qu’il attribue à la gouvernance du président de la République. Cette nouvelle campagne de proximité devrait dépasser les frontières guinéennes. Le mouvement compte aller à la rencontre des ressortissants guinéens installés dans plusieurs pays afin de partager son message et de renforcer les liens avec cette importante composante de la communauté nationale. Pour Oumar Sacko, la responsabilité dans la construction du pays incombe à l’ensemble des citoyens. Il appelle, dans cette perspective, à privilégier le dialogue, la tolérance et le respect des différences. Le président du MOSACCOD réaffirme par ailleurs sa reconnaissance au chef de l’État pour la confiance et l’attention accordées à son mouvement. Il assure que son organisation entend multiplier les initiatives afin d’accompagner la dynamique nationale et de contribuer à la préservation de la paix. À travers cette nouvelle orientation, le MOSACCOD veut donc passer d’une mobilisation principalement liée aux échéances électorales à une présence plus régulière sur le terrain, avec l’ambition affichée de participer aux débats et aux actions en faveur de la stabilité et du développement de la Guinée. L’article Après les élections, le MOSACCOD annonce une vaste tournée pour promouvoir la paix et les acquis du président Mamadi Doumbouya est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Troops arrest 3 alleged terrorist collaborators, destroy enclaves in Kaduna, Katsina
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have recorded operational successes in Kaduna and Katsina, with the arrest of 3 suspected terrorist collaborators, the interception of weapons and ammunition, as well as the destruction of identified terrorist enclaves during separate operations conducted on 27 and 28 August 2026. Lieutenant Col Aliyu Danja, Military Information Officer, made this known on Saturday, saying, “Troops of Sector 1 acted on information regarding the apprehension of a suspected terrorist collaborator in Kaduna State. “The suspect was found in possession of 2 locally fabricated guns and 13 rounds of ammunition concealed in a bag. “During preliminary investigation, the suspect disclosed that he had been tasked to deliver the weapons and ammunition to another individual. “Acting on the information from the suspect, troops swiftly conducted a follow-up operation and apprehended 2 additional suspects connected with the movement of the weapons. “The 3 suspects, along with the recovered weapons, ammunition and other items, are currently undergoing further investigation. “In a separate operation on 28 August 2026, troops of Sector 2, supported by other security agencies, conducted clearance operation against identified terrorist enclaves around Maharba and Karaduwa in Matazu Local Government Area of Katsina State. “Troops successfully cleared and destroyed the enclaves and other structures used by the terrorists to support their criminal activities. “During the operation, troops also cleared and destroyed an enclave linked to notorious terrorist leader Kachalla Muhammadu Filani, whose group has been terrorizing innocent civilians in Matazu and Musawa Local Government Areas. “The terrorist leader narrowly escaped as troops advanced towards the enclave. Further exploitation of the area led to the recovery of an RPG-7 tube, a motorcycle, mobile phones and other items. “Troops thereafter conducted further fighting patrols within the general area to consolidate the gains and deny the terrorists freedom of action. “These successes underscore the sustained efforts of Operation Fansan Yamma to dismantle terrorist networks, disrupt the movement of weapons and other logistics, and deny terrorists the use of enclaves across the Joint Operations Area. “The Joint Task Force remains resolute in taking the fight to the terrorists through coordinated and intelligence-driven operations aimed at degrading their capabilities and restoring lasting peace and security to affected communities.” The post Troops arrest 3 alleged terrorist collaborators, destroy enclaves in Kaduna, Katsina appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Création de l’UGB de Saint-Louis : Ndar aussi dit Lux mea lex
items.description: Elle fait sa route et ses fiertés, donne au Sénégal ministres et autres cadres de la République. On dit Sanar. Et ce mot, prononcé, dit une terre de savoirs dans une ville de Saint-Louis déjà pleine d’histoires. Son histoire, quant à elle, remonte à la deuxième moitié du siècle dernier. Le 14 janvier 1975, Léopold Sédar Senghor posait une première pierre. Marien Ngouabi, son homologue congolais, accompagné de son épouse et en visite officielle au Sénégal du 12 au 15, était alors aux côtés du poète-président, lorsqu’avec la pierre, ce dernier signait l’acte de naissance de ce qui deviendra l’Université Gaston Berger de Saint-Louis. A lire aussi : Formation et soft skills: L’Ugb renforce le leadership étudiant avec une deuxième cohorte de formateurs « Après Dakar, après l’École polytechnique de Thiès, c’est la métropole des bords du Fleuve qui accueille l’élite de notre jeunesse. Ici, comme ailleurs, s’affirmera la vocation de toute Université nationale digne de ce nom et demeurera valide la devise de notre université, Lux mea lex ». Ainsi s’était exprimé le ministre sénégalais de l’enseignement supérieur, M. Ousmane Camara, dans un discours rapporté par Le Soleil du 15 janvier 1975. L’Ugb, dès sa naissance, a porté les valeurs d’ouverture et de Téranga caractéristiques du Sénégal. Et bien saint-louisiennes. « Cette université sera ouverte aux étudiants des pays de la région », peut-on lire, comme titre du discours retranscrit dans le papier de janvier 1975. En majuscules… Université Gaston Berger de Saint-Louis, cette appellation, en remplacement d’« université de Saint-Louis », est adoptée le 4 décembre 1996 par le décret nᵒ 96-1016. Ce qui s’abrège aujourd’hui UGB et a fondu son nom dans celui de Sanar (localité saint-louisienne qui l’abrite) sera officiellement inauguré par un président autre que celui qui en a posé la première pierre. C’est en effet Monsieur Abdou Diouf qui aura cet honneur. Ndar, le 27 février 1997… Cet autre temple du savoir n’a certes pas attendu 97 et son ouverture officielle pour donner ses premiers cours ! Quinze ans après 75, le 2 janvier 1990 plus précisément, la loi n° 90-03 la créait. Le 17 décembre 1990, grand jour ! « Les étudiants qui ont passé la journée du lundi à s'inscrire et subir des visites médicales, déclarent eux-mêmes qu'ils ont été bien accueillis. Le corps professoral est également en place… », disait Le Soleil. La deuxième université du Sénégal, après celle de Dakar, accueillait ainsi ses 600 étudiants. Par Moussa Seck

items.title: Jeux méditerranéens : la boxe marocaine « écrit l’histoire » avec deux médailles d’or
items.description: La sélection marocaine de boxe « a écrit l'histoire » aux Jeux méditerranéens (Tarente 2026), en décrochant six médailles, dont deux en or, a affirmé, vendredi soir, le directeur technique national (DTN) à la Fédération Royale Marocaine de Boxe (FRMB), Gabriele Martelli. Dans une déclaration à la presse à l’arrivée de la délégation marocaine à l’aéroport international Mohammed V de Casablanca, M. Martelli a mis en avant les deux titres remportés par Saïda Lahmidi (-70 kg) et Soulaimane Samghouli (-65 kg) ainsi que la médaille d’argent de Widad Bertal (-54 kg) et les trois médailles de bronze décrochées par Mounia Toutir (-65 kg), Yasmine Mouttaki (-51 kg) et Abdelhak Nadir (-70 kg) . Le DTN a souligné que ces performances ont été réalisées après seulement deux mois de préparation, relevant que le travail mené avec les athlètes marocains repose sur une méthodologie exigeante intégrant la discipline, la préparation psychologique, la nutrition et la préparation physique. Il a, dans ce sens, fait part de l’ambition de poursuivre cette dynamique à travers un vaste plan de développement de la boxe nationale, avec l’objectif d’améliorer les performances des pugilistes marocains et de « marquer l’histoire année après année ». De son côté, le vice-président de la FRMB, Nabil Hilmi, a qualifié cette participation d’ »exceptionnelle », aussi bien par le nombre que par la qualité des médailles obtenues, rappelant que le Maroc n’avait plus décroché deux médailles d’or lors d’une même édition des Jeux méditerranéens depuis 1987. Il a également relevé la portée particulière de la médaille d’or féminine remportée par Saïda Lahmidi, une première pour la boxe marocaine dans cette compétition, estimant que les résultats enregistrés à Tarente constituent un indicateur positif quant au niveau de préparation de l’équipe nationale pour les prochaines échéances. M. Hilmi a précisé que ces Jeux représentent une étape importante dans la préparation aux prochains rendez-vous internationaux, notamment le Championnat du monde, le Championnat d’Afrique et les échéances africaines qualificatives pour les Jeux Olympiques. Pour sa part, la médaillée d’or Saïda Lahmidi s’est dite particulièrement heureuse de cette consécration, obtenue au terme d’une compétition qu’elle a qualifiée de « très difficile », soulignant que la solidarité et la cohésion au sein de l'équipe nationale ont joué un rôle important dans la réalisation de cette performance. Elle a attribué ce résultat aux efforts consentis lors des stages de préparation, saluant l'appui de la FRMB, du DTN et de l’ensemble des cadres techniques, avant de dédier sa victoire à sa famille et aux Marocains qui ont soutenu la sélection nationale. Même son de cloche chez Soulaimane Samghouli, médaillé d’or dans la catégorie des moins de 65 kg, qui a exprimé sa grande satisfaction après ce sacre, soulignant le niveau relevé de la compétition, marquée par la participation de plusieurs nations de référence dans cette discipline. Les compétitions de boxe des Jeux méditerranéens de Tarente se sont achevées jeudi, permettant au Maroc de terminer à la troisième place du tableau des médailles de la discipline, derrière l’Espagne, première, et l’Italie, pays organisateur, deuxième. The post Jeux méditerranéens : la boxe marocaine « écrit l’histoire » avec deux médailles d’or appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Kano-Katsina rail project 80% complete — FG
items.description: By Nnasom David The federal government has reaffirmed its determination to complete and commission the 284-kilometre Kano-Katsina railway project by December 2026, despite challenges earlier posed by insecurity, land disputes and the seasonal slowdown in construction activities. The assurance was given during a joint inspection of the project by officials of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Federal Ministry of Finance, representatives of lending institutions and the project contractor. The inspection provided an update on the progress of the strategic rail corridor, with officials putting the level of physical completion at 80 per cent. Speaking shortly after the inspection, the permanent secretary, Ministry of Transportation, Engr. Funso Adebiyi, represented by the Director, Rail Transport Services, Engr. Habibat Buhari, said the project remained firmly on course despite some setbacks. She said the rainy season had slowed construction activities slightly, but stressed that significant work had already been accomplished. Buhari explained that the current level of physical progress remained around 80 per cent, adding that materials required for track laying had already been stockpiled at the project camp. According to her, the government was working to ensure that the remaining activities were completed within the approved timeline. “We have done a lot of work for just one per cent physical progress,” she said, stressing that the project had reached a stage where major construction activities could be accelerated. The representative of the permanent secretary identified insecurity in some sections of the corridor and disputes over land and canal areas as the two major issues affecting the pace of construction. She explained that security concerns had disrupted day-to-day activities in some areas, while some communities were yet to accept provisions relating to the Land Use Act. She, however, assured that the challenges would only delay the project temporarily and would not stop its completion. “These will only cause delays, not stop the project. We have had similar cases in the past and they have been attended to,” she said. She also disclosed that the government was intensifying engagement with affected communities and other stakeholders to resolve the land-related disputes and enable contractors to move into the affected sections. She expressed confidence that the December commissioning target would be achieved. She also said efforts were being made to ensure that the required rolling stock arrived in time for the commissioning. “Even if we don’t get all of it, at least we get the ones to commission by December. We are targeting the commissioning of the project by December, God willing, and there is no going back. So we are on course,” she stated. Also speaking, a representative of the Ministry of Finance, the director of the Office of the Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Finance, Alhaji Muhammadu Kamal, said government releases were being made as and when due and the federal government has released its 15 per cent counterpart funding. He said the level of work already completed demonstrated the federal government’s commitment to fulfilling its financial obligations under the project agreement. He explained that the project was being financed through a combination of loan facilities and counterpart funding, with the federal government responsible for 15 per cent of the project financing while 85 per cent was covered by the financing facility. The Senior Country Officer and representative of the Development Bank of Southern Africa, Siya Biniza, disclosed that the bank had invested about $250 million in the project. Biniza described the railway as a strategic infrastructure investment with significant potential economic benefits for northern Nigeria and the wider region. He said the inspection demonstrated that substantial financial resources had already been committed to the project. Meanwhile, the contractor, Mota-Engil Nigeria, also reaffirmed its commitment to delivering the Kano-Katsina section by December 2026. Representing the company and speaking in his capacity as chief financial officer, Vladislav Bystrenko said the first phase of the project, covering the Kano-Katsina corridor, was expected to be completed by December. He disclosed that the extension from Katsina to Maradi in Niger Republic was expected to be completed by the end of 2027. According to him, the project had reached approximately 80 per cent completion. The post Kano-Katsina rail project 80% complete — FG appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Police detain officers over fatal shooting of driver in Rivers
items.description: The Police Command in Rivers says it has detained some officers over the alleged shooting and killing of a commercial driver in Port Harcourt. The command’s spokesperson, ASP Blessing Agabe, disclosed this while briefing journalists in Port Harcourt on Friday. Agabe said the incident occurred on Thursday after an altercation between the driver, identified as Anthony Obodo, and a police officer. According to her, the altercation degenerated into a scuffle, during which one of the officers allegedly fired a shot. She said the bullet struck Obodo, killing him, while two other passers-by sustained injuries during the incident. “Preliminary information indicates that an altercation occurred between the occupant and the officers, leading to a scuffle and subsequent gunshot,” she said. Agabe identified the alleged shooter as Cpl. Alfred Louis, who was subsequently attacked and assaulted by an angry mob. She said Louis sustained multiple injuries during the attack and was receiving attention while investigations continued. The spokesperson said Louis and members of his team had been detained at the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID). “The investigation will establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and determine the appropriate disciplinary action in accordance with the law,” she said. Agabe condemned Obodo’s killing, saying the alleged shooting did not reflect professionalism expected in policing. She said the command would not relent in taking disciplinary action against officers found culpable of unethical or unlawful conduct. “The command will not shield any officer engaging in unethical and unlawful conduct that brings the Nigeria Police Force into disrepute,” she said. The spokesperson assured the public that the investigation would be conducted in accordance with the law and relevant disciplinary procedures. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the incident sparked widespread protests across Rivers on Friday. Police operatives were subsequently deployed across affected areas to restore law and order and prevent further breakdown of public peace. (NAN) The post Police detain officers over fatal shooting of driver in Rivers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FG sets up task force over diphtheria outbreak in Katsina, Kano
items.description: The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Pate, has activated an emergency task force to contain the diphtheria outbreak among children in parts of Katsina and Kano States. This is contained in a statement on Friday in Abuja by Ado Bako, Assistant Director, Information and Public Relations, Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare. It said the ministry constituted the task force in collaboration with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA), affected states and international partners. It said the measure was to strengthen surveillance, close immunisation gaps and ensure timely access to treatment. “As part of the immediate response, NPHCDA has deployed 500,000 doses of vaccines to Katsina and Kano States to support intensified immunisation activities in affected and at-risk communities.” According to the statement, the task force would be co-chaired by the Director-General of NCDC and the Director of Public Health, with members drawn from NPHCDA, Commissioners for Health in Katsina, Kano, Zamfara and Sokoto States, WHO, UNICEF and the National Tuberculosis and Leprosy Control Programme in Katsina. It said the ministry’s Chief Epidemiologist will serve as Secretary of the task force. It said the task force had been directed to immediately strengthen outbreak investigation and disease surveillance, intensify community sensitisation and immunise unvaccinated children in affected and at-risk communities. The statement added that the task force would work with the Katsina State Government to establish treatment annexes in hospitals across the state’s three senatorial districts — Katsina, Daura and Funtua. It further said urgent support would be mobilised to the Federal Teaching Hospital, Katsina, the principal referral centre for the state and parts of neighbouring states. It said the support would include Diphtheria Antitoxin (DAT), intravenous antibiotics, additional clinical personnel and personal protective equipment (PPE). According to the statement, the task force will provide weekly updates to the Coordinating Minister on progress, emerging challenges and additional requirements. It said identified bottlenecks would be escalated for immediate resolution, adding that the Federal Government remained committed to protecting Nigerian children from vaccine-preventable diseases. It also reaffirmed the government’s commitment to a swift, coordinated and evidence-based response to bring the outbreak under control. (NAN) The post FG sets up task force over diphtheria outbreak in Katsina, Kano appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Élections territoriales au Sénégal : cinq reports dénombrés depuis 1984
items.description: Les élections territoriales ont été rarement organisées à date échue. Cinq reports de 1984 à nos jours ont été dénombrés. Et à chaque fois, des arguments ne manquent pas pour justifier le chamboulement. Les élections territoriales au Sénégal ont souvent été reportées. Le renouvellement des exécutifs locaux (maires, présidents de Conseil départemental, conseillers municipaux et départementaux) suscite chaque fois des débats. Depuis plusieurs années, le débat sur le report des territoriales semble être un marronnier politique. Il est de plus en plus agité depuis quelques semaines, le mandat des maires et présidents de Conseil départemental élus en janvier 2022 devant arriver à terme dans quelques mois, notamment en début 2027. Ce même débat était posé aussi en 2019, date de fin de mandat des exécutifs territoriaux élus en 2014. Initialement prévues en juillet 2019, les élections territoriales ont été reportées en décembre 2019 avant d’être reportées encore une fois jusqu’au plus tard en mars 2021. Finalement, elles ont été organisées en janvier 2022. L’historique de ces élections locales renseigne que depuis plus de 40 ans, le calendrier électoral sénégalais n’a cessé d’être réajusté. La réflexion sur ce report systématique des locales a été menée par plusieurs organisations de la société civile depuis 2019. Dans leur document intitulé, « Mémorandum de la Société civile sénégalaise sur le report des élections et la prorogation du mandat des conseillers départementaux et municipaux », le constat qui s’était dégagé est que depuis 1984 les élections locales sont soumises à une « légalité dérogatoire ». Il y a eu au moins 5 reports du scrutin local. Le document dont nous avons copie avait rappelé qu’en 1984, les élections locales n’ont pas été organisées à la date initialement prévue, elles ont été tenues qu’après la généralisation des communes de plein exercice. Prévues en 1995 aussi, ces élections furent reportées d’un an à cause de la politique de régionalisation enclenchée. La même logique fut poursuivie après 1996. Ces élections devaient se tenir en 2001, mais furent décalées d’un an suite à l’accession du président Abdoulaye Wade à la tête de la magistrature suprême, ainsi qu’à son désir d’expérimenter la provincialisation, comme nouvelle forme de décentralisation. Ce qui justifia la tenue des élections en 2002. D’après le même document de la société civile, cette pratique récurrente du report des élections va se poursuivre jusqu’en 2007. Les élections initialement prévues la même année furent reportées deux fois, en 2008 puis en 2009 à cause des contestations postélectorales de l’élection présidentielle de 2007 et du boycott des législatives par l’opposition. Après 2009, les élections territoriales sont tenues le 29 juin 2014, même si un report fut décidé pour une durée de 3 mois. En 2019, dans un contexte quasi similaire, il y a eu un premier report en décembre 2019, puis un deuxième report sans précédent, puisque non encadré. Finalement, les élections territoriales sont organisées en janvier 2022. Contrairement à ces reports des élections, la société civile avait souligné que la situation était un peu particulière pour 2019, car le projet de loi nᵒ 15/2019 portant report des élections prévues le 1ᵉʳ décembre 2019 et prorogation du mandat des conseillers départementaux et municipaux qui a été soumis à l’Assemblée nationale n’avait pas prévu de date fixe pour l’organisation desdites élections territoriales. Ainsi, Moundiaye Cissé de l’ONG 3D et compagnie avaient souligné qu’« il est à relever que le report des élections, procédure exceptionnelle, trouve son origine sous les différents régimes, avec les textes, mêlant droit et politique ». La jurisprudence du Conseil constitutionnel n’a jamais pu empêcher ces reports, qui se multiplient, essentiellement dans le cadre des élections locales et législatives, selon le mémorandum de la société civile. Compte tenu de la situation, ces spécialistes se demandent si « dans un État démocratique, la légalité dérogatoire doit-elle primer sur la légalité normale ? Pour les prochaines élections territoriales initialement attendues en 2027, l’opposition et les organisations de la société civile demandent le respect du calendrier électoral. Du côté du camp présidentiel, Aminata Touré avait affirmé il y a quelques semaines que le chef de l’État a encore du temps pour fixer la date des futures élections territoriales. Oumar KANDÉ

items.title: Police nab female students over viral assault video in Plateau
items.description: The Police Command in Plateau has arrested some female students over a viral video showing them allegedly attacking another female student in Pankshin Local Government Area. The Command spokesman, SP Alfred Alabo, disclosed this in a statement on Friday in Jos. Alabo said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ayodeji Faniyan, directed the Area Commander in Pankshin to investigate and arrest those involved immediately. “Immediately the CP got wind of it, he directed the Area Commander in Pankshin LGC to act immediately, which they have done,” he said. Alabo said the arrested students would be transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (CID) after preliminary investigations. He added that the suspects would subsequently be charged in court after the conclusion of investigations. He condemned the alleged attack, describing jungle justice and other forms of violence as criminal offences. He said recording and uploading violent acts on social media could also expose perpetrators to additional criminal charges, including cybercrime-related offences. “In the process of committing this crime, sometimes you will commit several other crimes, “It is not just you beating somebody or meting violence against your fellow human being; even having the mind to record it is cybercrime,” Alabo said. He urged youths and other residents to refrain from taking the law into their hands, irrespective of the circumstances surrounding any disagreement. “Learn to report to a third party that has the authority to hear your matter and give you the justice that you deserve,” he said. Alabo urged residents to report grievances and criminal incidents to the Police or other appropriate security agencies rather than resorting to violence. He also appealed to members of the public to continue providing timely and credible information to security agencies. He said such information would enable security agencies to promptly intervene and prevent situations from escalating. Alabo reiterated that the arrested students would be transferred to the State CID and subsequently charged in court after investigations. “Stay clear of jungle justice. Report cases anytime you are aggrieved to the right and appropriate authority,” Alabo said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the girls are students of the Federal University of Education in Pankshin. (NAN) The post Police nab female students over viral assault video in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Hydrocarbures, pétrochimie : le chinois Sinopec renforce ses positions en Algérie
items.description: Le groupe Sonatrach et le géant pétrolier chinois Sinopec renforcent leur partenariat avec la signature d’un protocole d’entente vendredi 28 août à Pékin. Selon le groupe pétrolier algérien, ce protocole d’entente porte les possibilités de coopération dans des domaines d’intérêt commun, tels que les « projets liés aux hydrocarbures conventionnels et non conventionnels, le développement des réservoirs complexes ainsi qu’à la pétrochimie et à l'hélium ». Le protocole d’entente entre Sonatrach et la compagnie chinoise porte aussi sur les « domaines de l’ingénierie pétrolière, des énergies renouvelables et des nouvelles technologies associées ainsi que le développement des compétences », a précisé Sonatrach dans un communiqué. Le protocole d’entente en marge de la visite que le PDG de Sonatrach, Nour Eddine Daoudi, effectue en Chine. Sinopec renforce ses positions en Algérie « Ce protocole s’inscrit dans la continuité des travaux et des actions menés dans le cadre du protocole d’entente signé en 2024 entre Sonatrach et Sinopec, dont les résultats ont permis d’identifier des opportunités d’intérêt mutuel et de mettre en œuvre des actions concrètes », explique le géant pétrolier et gazier algérien. Selon la plus grande compagnie d’Afrique, cet accord vise à « consolider les relations existantes entre les deux compagnies et à étendre leur coopération à travers la recherche de nouvelles opportunités de partenariat sur l’ensemble de la chaîne de valeur des hydrocarbures ». Ce protocole d’entente permet au géant pétrolier chinois de renforcer ses positions en Algérie où il a obtenu lundi 17 novembre 2025 un contrat de 437 millions de dollars pour la construction d'une unité d'hydrotraitement de naphta lourd au niveau de sa raffinerie située dans la ville d’Arzew près d’Oran. Le même mois, Sinopec a obtenu, en partenariat avec Sonatrach, un permis d’exploitation d’hydrocarbures au niveau du gisement de Guern el Guessa II. L’article Hydrocarbures, pétrochimie : le chinois Sinopec renforce ses positions en Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Two Nigerians extradited to US over schemes linked to teenagers’ deaths
items.description: Two Nigerians have been extradited to the United States to face federal prosecution over alleged financially motivated sextortion schemes targeting American minors. The suspects, Adebola Festus Adekunle, 26, and Mudasiru Afeez Olawale, 24, were arrested in Nigeria in August 2023 following an international operation led by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). They were extradited on Thursday and appeared separately in federal courts in Mississippi and North Carolina on Friday, the U.S. Department of Justice said. Adekunle and Olawale are presumed innocent unless and until prosecutors prove the charges against them beyond reasonable doubt in court. The extraditions followed years of cooperation between U.S. investigators and Nigerian authorities after the suspects were arrested separately in August 2023, the U.S. Department of Justice said. The department particularly acknowledged Nigeria’s Attorney-General and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagnemi (SAN), the Federal Ministry of Justice and the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission. It described the support and assistance provided by Nigerian security authorities as “essential” to successfully bringing the suspects before American courts. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs and the FBI Legal Attaché Office in Abuja were also involved in coordinating the international transfer. FBI Director, Kash Patel, on Friday, described the suspects as “two high-value targets” returned to American soil through international law-enforcement cooperation. “Two Nigerian subjects arrested in Nigeria in 2023 – Adebola Festus Adekunle and Mudasiru Afeez Olawale – have now been returned to the United States,” Patel said. He said they would face justice after allegedly participating in financially motivated sextortion of minors, with the cases involving devastating consequences for young victims. “They’ve been overseas for three years but this FBI and our DOJ (Department of Justice) partners went and got them,” Patel said. He described sextortion as a particularly dangerous crime because perpetrators frequently target vulnerable young people through deception, intimidation and threats. “Sextortion is a heinous crime targeting innocent people, often young children,” the FBI Director said. Financially motivated sextortion typically involves offenders deceiving victims online into providing intimate images before threatening to circulate them unless money is paid. The FBI says perpetrators often impersonate young people online and approach victims through social-media platforms, messaging applications, online games and other digital communication services. The FBI warned that the crime can escalate extremely rapidly and leave victims experiencing intense fear, humiliation and psychological distress. U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said both suspects were arrested in Nigeria during a wider operation targeting alleged sextortionists preying on minors in the United States. “The defendants were arrested in Nigeria as part of a wider operation with the FBI to apprehend sexual extortionists targeting minors in the United States,” Blanche said. He said Washington had strengthened international law-enforcement partnerships to dismantle foreign criminal networks allegedly involved in financially motivated sextortion. The Attorney General said such networks had been linked to “dozens of American teen deaths by suicide,” underscoring the growing international concern surrounding the crime. The cases form part of Operation Artemis, an FBI initiative targeting financially motivated sextortion networks operating from Nigeria. Under the operation, U.S. authorities deployed agents, analysts and forensic specialists to Nigeria to work alongside international and domestic law-enforcement partners. (NAN) The post Two Nigerians extradited to US over schemes linked to teenagers’ deaths appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Drame de Ben Guerdane | Rassemblement à Paris en solidarité avec les familles des victimes
items.description: Après le drame de Ben Guerdane, des activistes tunisiens en France organisent un rassemblement de solidarité avec les familles des victimes sous le slogan «De Ben Guerdane à Paris : nos vies ont la même valeur», et ce, le dimanche 30 août à 14heures à la Fontaine des Innocents, Châtelet, Paris. Quinze jeunes ont pris la mer à la recherche d’un avenir. Douze corps ont été retrouvés, deux jeunes sont toujours portés disparus et un seul a survécu, après deux jours et deux nuits en Méditerranée. Derrière ces chiffres, il y a des vies, des familles, des rêves et une jeunesse qui demande simplement le droit de vivre dignement et d’espérer. Cette mobilisation est une initiative citoyenne de Tunisiennes et Tunisiens résidant à l’étranger «Tunisiennes et Tunisiens contre le Racisme» . Elle n’appartient à aucun parti et ne se place sous aucune bannière politique. «Nous refusons de rester silencieux. Nous nous rassemblons pour défendre les droits humains, la dignité, l’égalité et le droit à la vie, et pour dire clairement notre refus de toutes les formes de racisme, de discrimination et de déshumanisation des personnes migrantes, quelles que soient leur origine, leur nationalité ou la couleur de leur peau» , affirment les organisateurs dans un appel au rassemblement. Ils ajoutent : «Nous refusons que la Méditerranée continue d’être un cimetière. Nous refusons que la migration soit traitée uniquement à travers les frontières, les contrôles, les bateaux et les accords sécuritaires. Nous demandons des politiques qui donnent aux jeunes des perspectives : emploi, développement, dignité et voies de mobilité sûres et légales.» «La responsabilité est partagée. La Tunisie comme l’Europe doivent assumer leurs responsabilités. La protection des frontières ne peut jamais avoir plus de valeur que la protection des vies humaines» , affirment-ils encore, tout en appelant les Tunisiennes et Tunisiens de France, mais aussi toutes les citoyennes et tous les citoyens de Paris et de ses alentours qui partagent ces valeurs, les associations, les syndicats, les défenseurs des droits humains et toutes les personnes refusant le racisme et l’indifférence, à les rejoindre lors du rassemblement prévu dans la capitale française. «Parce qu’une vie tunisienne, africaine, européenne ou d’ailleurs a exactement la même valeur. Nos jeunes rêvent d’avenir : Tunisie et Europe, ne les condamnez pas à mourir. De Ben Guerdane à l’Europe, que la Méditerranée relie nos vies, qu’elle ne les engloutisse plus» , concluent-ils. L’article Drame de Ben Guerdane | Rassemblement à Paris en solidarité avec les familles des victimes est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: ‘You cannot defend Prophet Mohammed with violence’ — Ameer warns Muslims
items.description: A call by the Ameer and Missionary-in-Charge of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Mission Ghana, Alhaji Maulvi Noor Mohammed Bin Salih, for religious restraint has assumed added significance following a recent chain of events involving an imam, a pastor and the alleged assault of the pastor while in police custody. Speaking at the Majlis Ansarullah (Elders) gathering at Nasrat Jahan in Wa in the Upper West Region, Alhaji Bin Salih urged Muslims and Ghanaians generally not to respond to religious provocation with insults or violence. His appeal came against the backdrop of heightened public discussion over religious tolerance after the arrest of an imam who allegedly called for violence against persons who insulted Prophet Mohammed, followed by the arrest of a pastor over alleged derogatory comments about the Prophet. The controversy escalated when a Muslim man was captured in a viral video slapping the handcuffed pastor at the Ghana Police Service Headquarters in Accra. The Ghana Police Service subsequently arrested the man, who was captured in the video assaulting the pastor. He was taken into custody to assist with investigations. The incident also triggered concerns about how a civilian gained access to a suspect who was already in police custody. ‘You cannot defend the Prophet’ It was against that backdrop that Alhaji Bin Salih appealed to Ahmadi Muslims to exercise restraint, particularly when confronted with statements they considered offensive to their faith. “You cannot defend the Holy Prophet Muhammad. Even the Almighty God who sent him watched on when the Holy Prophet was insulted, vilified in his own lifetime,” he said. He urged Muslims to draw lessons from the conduct of the Prophet rather than resorting to retaliation. Citing the experience of the Prophet at Ta’if, where he was reportedly stoned by its people, the Ameer said the Prophet rejected an offer by an angel to punish those responsible. “Even in Ta’if when he was stoned mercilessly and the angel appeared asking to assist him to punish them, he said, No, don’t do that. If you do that, who will worship God tomorrow? He said these very people and their children will worship God tomorrow.” He said the Prophet’s response demonstrated that forgiveness and restraint could be more powerful than retaliation. Alhaji Bin Salih also cited the Prophet’s conduct following the Conquest of Makkah, when he forgave those who had previously persecuted him and his followers. “When Makka fell, what was his message? ‘La Tathriba Alaykumul Yaum’ — No blame on you today. Those of you who think we will retaliate for atrocities you carried out against us, forget it. Nothing like that will happen. You are free.” The Ameer said Ghana had for generations demonstrated that Muslims and Christians could live together peacefully, often within the same families, compound houses and communities. He questioned why religious differences should now become a source of confrontation. “In Ghana we live communally. There is no family in Ghana you will not find a Muslim and also a Christian. No family. There is no compound house you enter, whether rented or family house, you will not find that this door is a Muslim’s room and the next door is a Christian’s room. We’ve coexisted how many years now? What is the new thing we have discovered that we have decided to turn against each other and use religion to destroy ourselves?” His warning comes at a time when social media has increasingly become a vehicle for the rapid circulation of religiously provocative statements, videos and counter-reactions. The recent controversy has demonstrated how quickly provocative religious commentary can move from online platforms into real-world confrontation, prompting interventions by the police, religious leaders and the Interior Ministry. A subsequent meeting between religious leaders and the police brought together the imam, the pastor and the man accused of assaulting the pastor in an effort to de-escalate tensions. The three men were later seen embracing in a gesture interpreted as a call for forgiveness and peaceful coexistence. For Alhaji Bin Salih, however, the responsibility for protecting Ghana’s peace extends beyond religious leaders and security agencies to ordinary citizens. He urged the elders of the Ahmadiyya Muslim Community to lead by example and ensure that messages of tolerance and peaceful coexistence were passed on to younger generations. “We must know that we have a mission for this country. The future of this country is in our hands. If the country fails, we sitting down here are the ones who have failed the country.”
